assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Fails if review dispatch is omitted, targets the superseded revision, dispatches the still-conflicting case, or duplicates either clean request.
Fails if the persisted pending landing retains the original head instead of the independently read Git repair head.
Fails if a repair is published before any fresh review is stored; removing the new review wait restores this regression.
Fails if a clean exact-head review never releases the pending repair to main.
Fails if remote publication omits or changes the clean.py content committed before landing; this independently verifies content rather than ancestry alone.
Fails if successful publication leaves its pending-landing journal behind.
Fails if publication leaves the delivered repair attempt live.

assertion_analysis.assertion: any((row['status'] == 'finished' and row['head'] == clean['head'] for row in result['interrupted_landings']))
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Fails if the completion receipt omits finished status or cites the original revision rather than the independently created repair head.
Fails if either refusal is omitted or duplicated in the returned obligations.
Fails if the blocked-review obligation omits the review cause.
Fails if the obligation loses the concrete stored blocking finding.
Fails if the still-conflicting obligation omits its conflict cause.
Fails if either refused repair pointer does not persist a refused landing status.
Fails if either persisted refusal cites the original revision instead of the Git-derived repair head.
Fails if a persisted refusal has no actionable guard text.
Fails if the repaired head with a blocking exact-head review is nevertheless merged.
Fails if the still-conflicting repaired head is treated as published.
Fails if consuming stored review results launches extra duplicate reviews.
Fails if the existing classifier rejects promoted repair review dispatch as not scoring, as observed at base.
Fails if direct dispatch composes the wrong run or original head; the expected head is read from git before dispatch, not supplied as a dispatch head argument.
Fails if a review of the original revision authorizes repair publication rather than an exact-head review wait.
Fails if a superseded review prevents requesting the current Git head or causes a wrong-head composition.
Fails if the repaired head is published with only a superseded-head review.
Fails if a gate log lacking terminal EXIT is accepted instead of producing repair-gate-refused; this guard already worked at base.
Fails if an incomplete repair gate nevertheless launches a review.
Fails if an incomplete repair gate nevertheless publishes the repaired head.

assertion_independence: All 26 assertions have a named falsifying condition; no added assertion merely echoes a head supplied to the operation under test: the expected repairs come from git rev-parse and differ from the original head initially written into pending records.
